introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0565 Human Biology 1, June 2024, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; select only one answer. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one best answer, A, B, C or D. For questions 24 to 27, choose A if 1, 2 and 3 are all correct; B if 1 and 2 are correct; C if 2 and 3 are correct; D if 1 only is correct.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which characteristic makes man a mammal?
questions.corrige_markdown: Mammals are defined by features such as hair, mammary glands, an external ear (pinna), a diaphragm and teeth of different types (heterodont dentition: incisors, canines, premolars and molars). An erect posture and opposable thumbs are features of man and other primates only, and a four-chambered heart is also found in birds, so none of these three defines a mammal. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: He has a four- chambered heart

questions.enonce_markdown: Simple diffusion differs from active transport in that:
questions.corrige_markdown: Simple diffusion is passive: molecules move down the concentration gradient, from high to low concentration, without energy from the cell. Active transport moves substances against the gradient (low to high concentration) and needs energy from respiration, which is what options B, C and D describe. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: It moves molecules from an area of high to low concentration
It moves molecules from an area of low to high concentration
It is an active process that requires energy
It moves molecules against a concentration gradient

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the function of the mitochondrion in a cell?
questions.corrige_markdown: The mitochondrion is the site of aerobic respiration, where glucose is oxidised to release energy as ATP, so it is called the powerhouse of the cell. Lysosomes destroy worn-out organelles and carry out intracellular digestion, and ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the tissue type that underlies and supports other tissue types:
questions.corrige_markdown: Connective tissue (for example areolar tissue, bone, cartilage and blood) fills the spaces between organs and lies beneath epithelia, binding and supporting the other tissues. Epithelial tissue covers and lines surfaces, muscular tissue contracts and nervous tissue conducts impulses. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A cell which undergoes mitosis forms:
questions.corrige_markdown: Mitosis is one nuclear division that gives two daughter cells which are genetically identical to the parent cell and have the same chromosome number. Four cells that are genetically different (unidentical) are the result of meiosis, so options A, B and D are wrong. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which two minerals are necessary for bone ossification?
questions.corrige_markdown: Bone is hardened (ossified) by deposits of calcium phosphate, so calcium and phosphorus are the two minerals needed, together with vitamin D which helps calcium absorption. Iodine is needed for thyroxine, and sodium and magnesium are not the main bone minerals. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The biceps and triceps muscles are examples of which muscle type?
questions.corrige_markdown: The biceps and triceps are attached to bones by tendons and move the forearm at the elbow, so they are skeletal muscles (striated, under voluntary control). Smooth muscle is found in the gut and blood vessels, and cardiac muscle only in the heart. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
![fig-1](gce-ol-human-biology-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

The diagram below is that of the arm. (Courtesy of DG Mackeans; Introduction to Biology) Identify the joint Z.
questions.corrige_markdown: Joint Z is at the bottom of the upper arm, where the humerus meets the radius and ulna: it is the elbow. The elbow allows movement in one plane only (bending and straightening the forearm), which is typical of a hinge joint. Joint W at the top is the shoulder, a ball-and-socket joint. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the transmitter substance that is released into the synaptic cleft during the transmission of a nerve impulse;
questions.corrige_markdown: When an impulse reaches the end of the presynaptic neurone, vesicles release acetylcholine into the synaptic cleft; it diffuses across and starts an impulse in the next neurone. Cholinesterase (acetylcholinesterase) is the enzyme that breaks the transmitter down afterwards, so it is not the transmitter. Noradrenaline is used at some other synapses but acetylcholine is the standard answer. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a conditioned reflex?
questions.corrige_markdown: A conditioned reflex is a learned response in which a new stimulus (the bell) becomes linked by experience to an inborn response (salivation to food), as in Pavlov's dogs. The blink reflex and the withdrawal of the hand are inborn (simple) reflexes, and peristalsis is an involuntary movement of the gut. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Eye closes when a foreign object approaches it
Digested food moving along the gut by peristalsis
A dog salivating in response to ringing a bell
Hand taken up when pierced by a needle

questions.enonce_markdown:
![fig-2](gce-ol-human-biology-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

The diagram below shows the internal structure of the human ear. (Courtesy of Roland Soper; GCSCE Human Biology) What is the function of the part numbered 6?
questions.corrige_markdown: Part 6 is the coiled, snail-shaped cochlea, which contains the organ of Corti with the sensory cells that detect sound vibrations and send impulses along the auditory nerve (part 5). Equalising pressure is the job of the Eustachian tube (part 7), the ear ossicles amplify sound waves, and balance is maintained by the semicircular canals (part 4). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It equalizes the pressure between the ear drum and the atmosphere
It contains the organ for hearing

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the master gland of the endocrine System.
questions.corrige_markdown: The pituitary gland, at the base of the brain, is called the master gland because it secretes hormones that control other endocrine glands (thyroid, adrenals, gonads). The pancreas, thyroid and adrenals are controlled by it. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A hormone that prevents miscarriage in a pregnant woman is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Progesterone keeps the lining of the uterus thick and rich in blood vessels and stops uterine contractions during pregnancy, so it prevents miscarriage. Prolactin stimulates milk production, oestrogen repairs the uterine lining and LH causes ovulation. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A student carried out food tests on a food sample using Biuret's reagent and Benedict's solution. Purple and brick red colourations were produced. What food types were present in the food sample?
questions.corrige_markdown: Biuret's reagent turns purple (violet) in the presence of proteins. Benedict's solution, when heated, turns from blue to brick red with a reducing sugar. Starch is tested with iodine solution (blue-black), and a non-reducing sugar gives no colour change with Benedict's solution unless it is first hydrolysed. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the alimentary canal, where is bile produced?
questions.corrige_markdown: Bile is made continuously by the liver cells. It is stored and concentrated in the gall bladder and released into the duodenum through the bile duct. The common trap is option A, because the gall bladder only stores bile. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which enzyme in pancreatic juice catalyses the breakdown of starch into glucose?
questions.corrige_markdown: Pancreatic amylase is the carbohydrase that breaks down starch into smaller sugars (maltose), which are then completed to glucose by maltase. Pepsin and trypsin digest proteins, and erepsin (peptidases) finishes protein digestion in the small intestine. Amylase is the only enzyme listed that acts on starch. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the human tooth used for biting and cutting food.
questions.corrige_markdown: Incisors are the chisel-shaped front teeth used for biting and cutting. Canines tear food, and premolars and molars crush and grind it. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The volume of air which remains in the lung alveoli and air passages after a normal expiration is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Air that stays in the lungs and air passages and can never be expelled completely is the residual volume, which keeps the alveoli from collapsing. Tidal volume is the air moved in each normal breath, the inspiratory reserve volume is the extra air that can be breathed in, and the expiratory reserve volume is the extra air that can be forced out. Residual volume is the closest option to the description. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Aerobic respiration differs from anaerobic respiration in that:
questions.corrige_markdown: In aerobic respiration, glucose is oxidised completely to carbon dioxide and water, releasing much energy (about 38 ATP per glucose). In anaerobic respiration glucose is only partly broken down (to lactic acid in muscles, or to ethanol and carbon dioxide in yeast), which releases little energy. Options B, C and D describe anaerobic respiration or are not differences. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Glucose is completely breakdown into carbon dioxide and water
Glucose is partially breakdown into lactic acid and water
Its end products are toxic to the cells
It takes place in the cytoplasm of the cell

questions.enonce_markdown:
![fig-3](gce-ol-human-biology-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

The diagrams below show four different types of mammalian blood cells. (Courtesy of Roland Soper; GCSCE Human Biology) Which blood cell engulfs and destroys pathogens?
questions.corrige_markdown: Cell III has a lobed nucleus and granular cytoplasm: it is a phagocyte (neutrophil), a white blood cell that engulfs and digests pathogens by phagocytosis. Cell I is a red blood cell (biconcave, no nucleus), cell II is a group of platelets (cell fragments that help clotting) and cell IV is a lymphocyte, with a large round nucleus, which makes antibodies. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the human heart, the semi-lunar valves:
questions.corrige_markdown: The semi-lunar valves lie at the base of the aorta and the pulmonary artery. When the ventricles relax, they close and stop blood from flowing back into the ventricles. The tricuspid and bicuspid valves prevent backflow into the atria, and the valve tendons stop those valves from turning inside out. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Prevent backflow of blood into the right atrium
Prevent backflow of blood into the left atrium
Prevent the bicuspid valve from turning inside out when the left ventricle contracts
Prevent backflow of blood from the aorta and pulmonary artery into the left and right ventricles

questions.enonce_markdown: The fluid which bathes the body cells is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Tissue fluid (intercellular fluid) is the liquid that leaks out of the capillaries and surrounds the body cells, supplying them with oxygen and nutrients and collecting their wastes. Lymph is tissue fluid once it has entered the lymph vessels, plasma is inside the blood vessels and intracellular fluid is inside the cells. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Homeostasis can be defined as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a constant internal environment, that is the tissue fluid and blood, in terms of temperature, water, salts, glucose and so on. Options B, C and D name only one part of it (temperature, water or salts), so the most complete definition is A. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The maintenance of a constant body fluid composition
The maintenance of a constant body temperature
The maintenance of the water content of body fluids
The maintenance of the salt content of the body fluids

questions.enonce_markdown:
A rise in the human body temperature can be regulated by:

1. Vasodilation of the skin arterioles
2. Production of sweat by the sweat glands
3. Vasoconstriction of the skin arterioles
questions.corrige_markdown: When the body is too warm, the skin arterioles widen (vasodilation, statement 1), so more blood flows near the surface and loses heat, and the sweat glands produce sweat whose evaporation cools the skin (statement 2). Vasoconstriction (statement 3) narrows the arterioles to reduce heat loss in the cold, so it does not lower a raised temperature. Statements 1 and 2 are correct. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Natural active immunity:

1. Is acquired when a person is exposed to pathogens
2. Provides long- term protection against disease
3. Involves the production of memory cells
questions.corrige_markdown: Natural active immunity develops when the body meets a pathogen during an infection (statement 1), makes its own antibodies and memory cells (statement 3), and the memory cells give long-lasting protection because they respond quickly if the same pathogen returns (statement 2). All three statements are correct. Passive immunity (antibodies from the mother or a serum) is the type that gives only short protection. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Vasectomy as a birth control method:

1. Involves sterilization of the female by cutting and tying the oviducts
2. Involves sterilization of the male by cutting and tying the sperm ducts
3. Is highly reliable and effective
questions.corrige_markdown: Vasectomy is the surgical cutting and tying of the sperm ducts (vasa deferentia) of the male, so sperm can no longer reach the penis (statement 2), and it is one of the most reliable methods of contraception (statement 3). Cutting and tying the oviducts is the female operation called tubal ligation, so statement 1 is false. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The liver functions in:

1. The regulation of the blood glucose level
2. The regulation of the body temperature
3. The production of digestive juices

*Options as printed:* A) 1, 2, and 3 are all correct   B) 1 and 2 are correct   C) 2 and 3 are correct   D) 1 only is correct
questions.corrige_markdown:
The liver regulates the blood glucose level by converting excess glucose to glycogen (with insulin) and glycogen back to glucose (statement 1). It also makes bile, a digestive juice that emulsifies fats (statement 3), and its many chemical reactions release heat that helps to keep the body warm (statement 2, which many textbooks list as a liver function, although other textbooks give it only to the skin and the brain). Statements 1 and 3 are certainly correct, and the options do not offer '1 and 3', so the key depends on whether statement 2 is accepted.

**Intended answer: A (1, 2, and 3 are all correct).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The layer of the human skin which produces new cells by mitosis is the:
questions.corrige_markdown: The Malpighian (germinative) layer is the deepest layer of the epidermis. Its cells divide continually by mitosis and the new cells are pushed upward, where they become the granular layer and finally the dead, keratinised (cornified) layer. The dermis is below the epidermis and holds the blood vessels, nerves and glands. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the human kidney nephron, selective reabsorption of most useful components of the glomerular filtrate occurs in the:
questions.corrige_markdown: Ultrafiltration happens between the glomerulus and the Bowman's capsule. Most of the useful substances (all the glucose and amino acids, most of the water and salts) are then reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule, which has a brush border and many mitochondria. The collecting duct only adjusts the final water content of the urine. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A person who has both Anti-A and Anti-B antibodies in the blood plasma, belongs to
questions.corrige_markdown: A person with antigen A on the red cells makes anti-B only, a person with antigen B makes anti-A only, and a person with both antigens (AB) makes neither. Someone with both anti-A and anti-B antibodies has no A or B antigen, so the blood group is O. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Where does spermatogenesis and oogenesis occur in male and female humans, respectively?
questions.corrige_markdown: Sperm cells are made (spermatogenesis) in the seminiferous tubules of the testes of the male, and egg cells are produced (oogenesis) in the ovaries of the female. The order in the question is male first, then female, so the answer is testes and ovaries. Option A has the right organs in the wrong order. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Rising dampness in the walls of houses is due to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Rising damp is water from the ground that is drawn up into the walls by capillary action. It happens when the foundation has no damp-proof course (a waterproof layer such as bitumen or plastic sheeting) to stop it. Broken gutters, a defective roof and cracks let rain in from above or from the side, which is not rising dampness. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Lack of damp-proof course in the foundation of the house
Cracks in the walls of the house

questions.enonce_markdown: The process by which a mature ovary releases an egg cell into the oviduct is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Ovulation is the release of a mature egg (secondary oocyte) from a ripe Graafian follicle of the ovary into the oviduct. Oogenesis is the formation of egg cells, orgasm is the climax of sexual intercourse, and ogamy is not a reproductive process of this kind. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What happens to the body when salty food is eaten?
questions.corrige_markdown: Salty food adds salts to the blood, so the blood becomes more concentrated and its water potential falls, which means that its osmotic pressure rises. The osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus detect this, the person feels thirsty and the pituitary releases more ADH so that less water is lost in the urine. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Osmotic pressure of the blood falls
Osmotic pressure of the blood remains the same
Osmotic pressure of the blood rises

questions.enonce_markdown: Skin colour in humans can either be black or white. What does this statement describe?
questions.corrige_markdown: The phenotype is the observable characteristic of an organism, such as skin colour that can be seen (black or white). The genotype, the allele combinations and whether the organism is homozygous are about the genes and cannot be seen directly. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The homozygous nature of the organism
The allele combinations of the organism

questions.enonce_markdown: In the water cycle, which two processes add water to the atmosphere?
questions.corrige_markdown: Water enters the atmosphere as vapour by evaporation from oceans, lakes and the soil, and also when fuels are burnt (combustion produces water vapour). Precipitation and condensation take water out of the atmosphere, so options B and C are wrong, and absorption is not a process that adds vapour to the air. Evaporation and combustion is the only pair of which both processes add water vapour. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In humans, haemophilia is a recessive sex-linked trait. The probability of a carrier woman and a normal man having a haemophiliac son is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Let H be the normal allele and h the haemophilia allele, both on the X chromosome. Carrier woman: $X^H X^h$; normal man: $X^H Y$. The four equally likely children are $X^H X^H$ (normal girl), $X^H X^h$ (carrier girl), $X^H Y$ (normal boy) and $X^h Y$ (haemophiliac boy). One child out of four is a haemophiliac son, so the probability is 1/4. (Among the sons only, the chance would be 1/2, which is the trap in option A.) **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The immediate end products of photosynthesis in a green plant are:
questions.corrige_markdown: Photosynthesis is the process $6CO_2 + 6H_2O \rightarrow C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2$ in the presence of light and chlorophyll. The immediate products are glucose and oxygen; starch is made afterwards when glucose is converted for storage, and water is a raw material. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Groups of living organisms of the same species that occupy the same habitat form:
questions.corrige_markdown: A population is all the organisms of the same species living in the same habitat at the same time. A community is made up of all the populations of different species in a habitat, and an ecosystem is the community together with its non-living environment. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a symptom of cholera:
questions.corrige_markdown: Cholera, caused by the bacterium *Vibrio cholerae*, produces frequent, abundant watery diarrhoea (rice-water stools) with vomiting and rapid dehydration. Mucus and blood in the stool are typical of dysentery, and constipation is the opposite of the symptom. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In humans, albinism is a recessive trait. If the allele for normal skin colour is A and that for albinism is a. Which of the following genotypes will produce offspring in the ratio; 1/2 normal skin colour and 1/2 albinism?
questions.corrige_markdown: A 1:1 ratio is a test cross: a heterozygote (Aa) crossed with a homozygous recessive (aa). The heterozygote gives gametes A or a and the homozygous recessive gives only a, so the offspring are $Aa$, $Aa$, $aa$, $aa$, that is 1/2 normal (Aa) and 1/2 albino (aa). $Aa \times Aa$ gives 3 normal : 1 albino, while $AA \times Aa$ and $AA \times aa$ give only normal offspring. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the human male reproductive system, the structure that stores sperms while they develop is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: The epididymis is the coiled tube on the surface of each testis in which sperms mature and are stored until ejaculation. The testis makes the sperms, the scrotum is the bag of skin holding the testes and the penis delivers the semen. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the life cycle of the malaria parasite, the stage that attacks and destroys liver cells is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: The infective stage injected by the female *Anopheles* mosquito is the sporozoite. It travels in the blood to the liver and invades the liver cells, where it multiplies and finally destroys them. The merozoites that are later released attack red blood cells. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the primary treatment of sewage, the process of screening removes:
questions.corrige_markdown: In primary treatment, the sewage first passes through screens (grids) that remove large floating objects such as rags, plastics and wood. The grit and solids then settle in the sedimentation tank. Microbes are dealt with later by secondary treatment (biological) and by chlorination. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One biological reason for shaving pubic hair is to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Pubic hair can shelter ectoparasites such as pubic lice (crab lice), so shaving it is a hygienic measure. Looking attractive or presentable are not biological reasons, and shaving is not necessary for copulation. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One harmful effect of excessive alcohol consumption to the human body is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Alcohol prevents the release of ADH, so the kidneys produce a large volume of dilute urine and the body loses water (dehydration). Lung cancer is caused by tobacco smoke, and physical violence is a social effect on behaviour and not an effect on the body itself. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It increases the rate of heartbeat

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following fibres is ideal for making clothes to be used in cold weather conditions?
questions.corrige_markdown: Wool is a poor conductor of heat and traps air between its fibres, so it keeps the body warm. Cotton and linen are plant fibres that absorb sweat and are best for hot weather, and polyester is a synthetic fibre that does not insulate as well. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which hospital unit are people with highly infectious diseases taken care of?
questions.corrige_markdown: People with highly infectious diseases (for example cholera or Ebola) are kept apart from the other patients in an isolation ward, to stop the infection from spreading. The surgical ward is for operations, the emergency ward for urgent cases and the private ward for patients who pay for a single room. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One role of a reformatory school in a community is to:
questions.corrige_markdown: A reformatory school receives young offenders (delinquent children) and tries to reform them by education, counselling and training, so that they can return to society as responsible citizens. Prisons confine hardened criminals, and fighting poverty and promoting national integration are not the main role of such schools. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Nurture the minds of delinquent children

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify a first aid measure that can be administered to a victim of nose bleeding:
questions.corrige_markdown: For a nosebleed the victim sits down and leans the head slightly forward, pinching the soft part of the nose for about ten minutes, so that the blood runs out of the nose and is not swallowed or breathed into the lungs. Lifting the head back, blowing the nose (which breaks the clot) and moving around are wrong. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Instructing the victim to move around with the head lifted upwards
Instructing the victim to sit down and bend the head slightly forward
Instructing the victim to blow his or her nostrils immediately
Instructing the victim to lie down with the head tilted to one side
